rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a promising multimodal configuration with strong encoders (scvi_n200 for RNA, imagenet_vit_l for images) and effective aggregation/fusion strategies (transformer + weighted). This clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modal baselines and provides a strong baseline for future comparisons.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile) with weighted fusion achieves 0.725 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders and aggregation but uses concat fusion instead of weighted. It clarifies whether fusion method is critical for performance, a key design choice. This is a logical extension of the current promising direction while reducing uncertainty about a key hyperparameter.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal configurations with weighted fusion (config_001: 0.725) slightly outperform concat fusion (config_003: 0.721). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion consistent with config_001. This clarifies whether the image encoder choice impacts performance, balancing exploration of critical components (image encoder) with exploitation of the current best setup.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile configurations with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_001) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, maintaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion—key components from top-performing configs. It clarifies whether switching RNA encoders (scgpt vs scvi_n200) improves accuracy while keeping other effective settings, balancing exploration of RNA encoder choices with exploitation of proven aggregation/fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests the same RNA and image encoders but with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, directly comparing fusion methods. It clarifies whether the fusion strategy significantly impacts performance, balancing exploitation of the current top setup with exploration of alternative fusion approaches.

Existing evidence shows config_001 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from transformer to avgpool (while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method identical) could improve performance. It clarifies the importance of aggregation method, a key design choice, and explores a logical variation of the current top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows config_001 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). The uncertainty lies in whether the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 vs pca_n2000) significantly impacts performance. Testing config_011 (pca_n2000 RNA, same image encoder and other parameters) will clarify if the RNA encoder choice is critical. This balances exploration of key design choices while building on the current top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_001) yield the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with the same effective aggregation/fusion strategy could improve performance. It clarifies if encoder choices impact results while maintaining proven components, balancing exploration of encoder combinations with exploitation of known effective settings.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests a similar configuration but with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_036), which could clarify if the current best's aggregation/fusion choices are optimal. It balances exploration of aggregation methods while leveraging the strong RNA/image encoder combination from config_001.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same aggregation/fusion setup, clarifying if RNA encoder choice impacts performance. It balances exploitation (testing a similar high-performing setup) and exploration (testing a new encoder).
